extracted.intended_audience: writers, students, editors, and anyone seeking guidance on clear concise English prose
extracted.subtask_short: english style guide for clear writing
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and principles for writing clear, concise, and correct English prose — covering composition principles, grammar/usage/punctuation rules, matters of form, commonly misused words, and general stylistic advice for revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit needless words
rubrics_metrics.description: Vigorous writing is concise. Omit words that do not contribute meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate redundancy and unnecessary modifiers; shorten phrases (e.g., 'in order to' → 'to', 'a large number of' → 'many'); avoid padding sentences with fillers. Examples and edits in the text illustrate typical deletions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer active constructions to passive ones for directness and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the doer the subject when possible (e.g., 'The committee approved the measure' rather than 'The measure was approved by the committee'). Use passive only when the actor is unknown or deliberately deemphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put statements in positive form
rubrics_metrics.description: Make definite assertions rather than negations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State what is, not what is not (e.g., 'He was often late' rather than 'He was not often on time'); avoid weakening force with double negatives or hedged phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use definite, specific, concrete language
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose words that convey precise, concrete meaning instead of abstract vagueness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer specific nouns and verbs over abstractions and nominalizations; concrete detail strengthens writing and helps the reader form clear images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid a succession of loose sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not string too many short clauses with coordinating conjunctions; vary sentence types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix sentence structures and use subordinating constructions and punctuation to show relationships rather than piling 'and' or commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express coordinate ideas in similar form (parallelism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use parallel construction for items or phrases of equal importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure parallel grammatical form in lists and paired ideas (e.g., 'to read, to write, and to think,' not 'to read, writing, and to think'). Parallelism improves rhythm and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep related words together
rubrics_metrics.description: Place modifiers and qualifying phrases next to the words they modify to avoid ambiguity and misplaced modifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reorder sentence elements so adjectives, adverbs, and phrases clearly attach to their intended targets; check for dangling participles and awkward separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the paragraph the unit of composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paragraph should deal with a single topic or step in the development of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin paragraphs with a topic sentence or clear controlling idea; develop it with coherent sentences; use paragraph breaks to signal shifts in idea or emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a suitable design and hold to it
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the overall plan of a piece before writing and maintain appropriate structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide on the arrangement and order of points (chronological, topical, argumentative) and avoid wandering; revise for unity and progression of ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place the emphatic words of a sentence at the end
rubrics_metrics.description: Position words of strongest emphasis toward the sentence end for maximal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange clauses so that the most important information comes last; rephrase to move the focus appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: In summaries, keep to the action
rubrics_metrics.description: When summarizing, focus on principal events or actions rather than analysis or moralizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give only what the reader needs to follow, avoiding digressions or unnecessary commentary in summary passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and rewrite
rubrics_metrics.description: Good prose is produced by rethinking and pruning; revision is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut unnecessary words, reorder sentences and paragraphs, read aloud to detect awkward phrasing, and perform multiple passes to improve clarity, economy, and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fancy words and overelaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer simple, straightforward vocabulary to showy or pretentious diction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use rare or ornate words to impress; aim for naturalness and clarity. Avoid overwriting (excessive ornament) and overstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overstate
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid exaggeration and sweeping claims unsupported by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temper claims, choose precise qualifiers when needed, and avoid hyperbole that undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dialect except when essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Use dialect sparingly and only when it serves a clear purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive or caricatured dialect distracts and can mislead readers; use it only to reveal character or setting and do it sensitively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the comma in a series (Oxford comma)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a series of three or more terms with a single conjunction, place a comma after each term except the last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ the serial comma to prevent ambiguity and maintain clarity in lists (e.g., 'red, white, and blue').

rubrics_metrics.name: Form the possessive singular of nouns by adding 's
rubrics_metrics.description: Make singular nouns possessive with 's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply 's to singular nouns (e.g., 'the girl's book'); for classical names ending in s, usage guidance provided in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclose parenthetic expressions between commas
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commas to set off nonrestrictive or parenthetic material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert commas around clauses or phrases that are not essential to the sentence's meaning; do not use commas to set off restrictive elements that define the noun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place a comma before a coordinating conjunction joining independent clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: When two independent clauses are joined by and, but, or, etc., place a comma before the conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the comma to mark the conjunction joining full clauses (e.g., 'She left, and he stayed'); omit when the second element is not an independent clause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not join independent clauses with only a comma (avoid comma splice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not connect two full sentences with just a comma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a period, semicolon, or add a coordinating conjunction with a comma; alternatively, recast into subordinate clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the semicolon to join closely related independent clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: A semicolon connects clauses closely linked in thought without a conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ semicolons to emphasize relationship or to separate items in a list if those items contain internal commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the colon to introduce a list or amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Place a colon after an independent clause to introduce an explanation, quotation, or list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the clause before the colon is a complete sentence; do not use a colon where a comma or dash is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the dash for abrupt breaks or emphatic pauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Dashes mark sudden shifts or strong emphasis within a sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sparingly to indicate an abrupt change, an amplified thought, or parenthetical emphasis; do not overuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use hyphens in compound modifiers before a noun
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenate compound adjectives that precede a noun to avoid ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write 'well-known author' but not 'the author is well known'; follow conventional hyphenation rules and check usage in specific cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proper pronoun case
rubrics_metrics.description: Use subjective, objective, and possessive pronouns correctly according to their syntactic roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose 'he' vs. 'him', 'who' vs. 'whom' appropriately; test by substituting pronouns to determine correct case (e.g., 'between you and me', not 'you and I').

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe subject-verb agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure verbs agree in number with their subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the true subject (not intervening phrases) and match singular/plural; be careful with collective nouns and phrases starting with 'there' or 'here'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place commas to prevent misreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commas where omission would cause confusion or ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert commas to clarify meaning even if not strictly mandated by other rules; clarity takes precedence over pedantic omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words and expressions commonly misused
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid frequent misuses and choose correct idioms and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the list of commonly misused words/expressions in the book (examples include distinctions like 'which' vs. 'that', 'fewer' vs. 'less', and proper idiomatic usages). The book provides correct alternatives and brief explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: A few matters of form (titles, margins, quotations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventional formatting and presentation rules for manuscripts and printed material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice covers title capitalization, margins, the use of quotation marks and italics, abbreviations, and manuscript format; follow these simple form rules to present polished copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to style: prefer the standard and rewrite
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt standard idiom and revise for clarity, rhythm, and sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor familiar expressions over the offbeat or contrived; read prose aloud; discard overwrought phrases; choose words for fitness to context and ear. The book emphasizes continuous revision and sensitivity to idiom.
